title: What are the common factors of these five pairs?
description: Five pairs of numbers are written as primes, one above the other. Groups of primes that sit in both rows are multiplied, one is added, and the biggest is picked as the highest common factor. A check divides the first pair by its answer and finds that the results share no prime.
teaching_notes: One idea: shared groups of primes multiply to the common factors, a prime is used only as often as both numbers have it, and one is always common. Watch for students who say a pair with no shared prime has no common factor.

source: Figure it Out (common factors and HCF)
video_script.why: The child must find common factors and the highest common factor for five different pairs, including a pair with no shared prime and a pair where one number is a factor of the other.
video_script.substitution: Write each number as primes, multiply the groups of primes that sit in both, add the factor one, and pick the highest.
video_script.anchor: Each pair of numbers written as primes, one above the other.
video_script.payoff_line: The highest common factors are ten, five, one, seventy four and eighty one.

final_answer.spoken: the highest common factors are ten, five, one, seventy four and eighty one

maths_rules: 77 = 7 x 11. 725 = 5 x 5 x 29 (25 x 29 = 725). No prime in both. Common factor 1; HCF 1.
Check for 50 and 60: 50 / 10 = 5 and 60 / 10 = 6; 5 and 6 share no prime, so 10 is the highest.
Slip: when no prime is shared, 1 is still a common factor (the common factor list is never empty).
video_script.design: One idea: shared groups of primes, multiplied, give the common factors, and the biggest is the HCF. Assumes the worked pairs of the topic. Five pairs, one step each, then a check. Each pair stays on the board while it is solved.
